overview.summary: Prefix Sum is a technique that pre-calculates the cumulative sum of elements in an array to answer range sum queries in O(1) time.
learningObjectives: Understand how to build a prefix sum array in O(N) time.
Calculate the sum of any sub-array in O(1) time using subtraction.
Recognize when continuous subarray problems require this pattern.
overview.interviewRelevance: Prefix Sum turns O(N^2) brute-force nested loops into elegant O(N) linear time solutions.

paragraphs: Imagine you are tracking your total bank account balance every day. To find out exactly how much money you made between Day 3 and Day 10, you don't need to add up every single transaction in between.
You just take your total balance on Day 10 and subtract your total balance on Day 2. That single subtraction instantly gives you the sum of the range.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: By doing O(N) work once upfront, you can answer millions of range sum questions instantly in O(1) time.

definition.technicalDefinition: A Prefix Sum array is an array where the value at index `i` is the sum of all elements from index `0` to index `i` in the original array.

vocabulary.definition: Everything that comes before a certain point.
A request to find the sum of elements between two indices `[L, R]`.
Increasing or growing by successive additions.

keyProperties: Precomputation takes O(N) time and O(N) space.
Formula for Sum from index L to R: `Prefix[R] - Prefix[L-1]`

metaphor: A car's odometer. To find out how far you drove on a specific trip, you don't track every mile individually. You just subtract the starting mileage from the ending mileage.
mentalModel.clickSentence: Sum(L to R) = Sum(0 to R) - Sum(0 to L-1). We cut off the part we don't want.

memoryDescription: You create a new array `P` of the exact same length as the original array `A` (or length N+1 to cleanly handle edge cases).

operations.name: Build Prefix Array
operations.description: Iterate through the array once, keeping a running total.

code.python:
for i in range(len(arr)):
    prefix[i+1] = prefix[i] + arr[i]

operations.visualNote: A second array fills up beneath the first array, cell by cell.

operations.name: Range Query
operations.description: Subtract the prefix sum just BEFORE the start index from the prefix sum AT the end index.

code.python:
def query(L, R):
    return prefix[R+1] - prefix[L]

operations.visualNote: Instantly highlights two cells in the prefix array and subtracts them.

patternTemplate.whenToUse: Whenever you are asked to calculate the sum, product, or XOR of a contiguous subarray multiple times.

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: You are given an array of daily temperatures. You need to answer 100,000 queries asking for the average temperature between day L and day R.
recognitionQuiz.explanation: To answer 100,000 queries instantly, you need O(1) time per query. Prefix sum allows you to get the sum of any range instantly, which you can then divide by the number of days to get the average.

examples.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
examples.problemStatement: Given an integer array nums, handle multiple queries of the following type: Calculate the sum of the elements of nums between indices left and right inclusive.
steps: In the constructor, initialize a prefix array of size N + 1 with zeros.
Loop through the input array and populate the prefix array.
In the sumRange method, return `prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left]`.
examples.rationale: The N+1 sizing elegantly avoids out-of-bounds errors when querying from index 0.

conceptQuiz.question: Why do we often make the Prefix Sum array size N+1 instead of N?
options: To easily handle queries that start at index 0 without needing an 'if left == 0' edge case.
Because arrays must be even lengths.
To store the total length of the array at the end.
It is a requirement of Python.
conceptQuiz.explanation: If we want `Sum(0 to 5)`, the formula `Prefix[5] - Prefix[-1]` would crash or behave unexpectedly. Putting a dummy `0` at `Prefix[0]` makes the math `Prefix[6] - Prefix[0]` work perfectly.

conceptQuiz.question: Can Prefix Sum be used for multiplication instead of addition?
options: Yes, by storing cumulative products and dividing instead of subtracting.
No, it only works for addition.
Yes, but you subtract the products.
No, because numbers get too large.
conceptQuiz.explanation: Yes! You can do 'Prefix Product'. `Product(L to R) = Prefix[R] / Prefix[L-1]`. (Note: you have to handle zeros carefully!).
